22:51 Local Time, 09:51 GMT, 15:21 IST: Back in 2024, New Zealand brought an end to India's remarkable 12-year, 18-series unbeaten run in Test cricket at home. Now, India have returned the favour, snapping the Black Caps' own impressive streak of seven years and 11 consecutive bilateral ODI series victories on home soil. We are not suggesting that this carries the same magnitude as New Zealand's historic Test triumph, but it will certainly bring plenty of smiles to the Indian camp. Gautam Gambhir will be among those particularly pleased, having secured his first ODI series victory away from home as India's head coach. Interestingly, the last time New Zealand lost an ODI series at home was also against India, back in 2019.
Gurnoor Brar is the Player of the Series. He isn't here and the trophy is collected by Shreyas Iyer.

Santner (2/2): [Batting difficulties, inability to build momentum and the effectiveness of India’s bowling and field placements] I think it was, I think with the fields, it was a little bit two paced, the pitch. And I thought they squeezed us pretty well. And they made great use of the bounce as well. [Assessment of the 3-1 series result, competitive cricket, weather interruptions and opportunities for different players] You look at the scoreline 3-1. I think it was closer than that. We played some good cricket. Obviously had a little bit of rain around and lost a few tosses. But in between all that, there’s a lot of good stuff. I think today, even in the last game, if you could take it a little bit deeper, there’s obviously a lot of time, especially with the bat in 50-over cricket. And then, different guys coming in, it’s obviously good experience. Guys stepped up as well, which was nice.

Shreyas 2/2: [Appreciation for Indian supporters and record crowds attending the bilateral series in New Zealand] Absolutely, we’ve been seeing them coming in numbers and the way they have supported irrespective of the results, you know. It went in our way sometimes, it went in New Zealand’s way. They were supporting both the teams, which is very heartening to see. And this is the kind of support we need. And also the sport is growing to a different level. We know what kind of inspiration we get from them. So thanks a lot for the love and support to each and every one who have been here. [Mutual respect between India and New Zealand, on-field competition and off-field friendship] Yes, absolutely. I feel that that’s how it should be. Off the field should be friendly, but on the field it’s like a war.

Shreyas Iyer collects the trophy from BCCI honorary vice-president Rajeev Shukla before making his way back to the team and handing it over to Yash Thakur and Kumar Kushagra. The support staff join the players as the entire group gathers for the customary team photograph. A fairly muted celebration, but there are smiles all around, with everyone looking quite relaxed.

India may have sealed the series, but their batting frailties remain a significant talking point, particularly their ability to cope with challenging conditions. These are precisely the kind of surfaces they could encounter at the 2027 ODI World Cup, and the concerns will need addressing well before then. The third ODI was washed out, but across the other four matches, Virat Kohli was the only Indian batter to register a 50+ score in the series. India, though, will take plenty of satisfaction from getting the job done. It may not have been the most convincing of series victories, nor achieved in the manner they would have hoped, but winning an ODI series away from home is always special.

The limited-overs leg of the tour is now behind us, and the focus shifts to the red-ball battle, with the first of the two Tests beginning on November 19. A different format, a fresh challenge and plenty at stake, with crucial World Test Championship points up for grabs. So, to all our viewers in India, get some rest and recharge your batteries.
